articles.title: Welcome to SJAA New Officers and Program Leaders
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) announces its new officers and program leaders, including Aaron Nair as Vice-President and Secretary, Jon Anderson for School Star Parties, Rich Jasper for Donations, and Joe Fragola for Starry Nights. The article highlights their diverse professional backgrounds and shared passion for astronomy, often rekindled later in life, and their commitment to contributing to the community and inspiring future generations. Many express a lifelong dedication to space science and sharing the wonders of the night sky.

articles.title: Thank You JVN!
articles.summary: This article is a heartfelt tribute to Jim Van Nuland (JVN), a dedicated, long-time member of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It celebrates his extensive service in various leadership roles, his passion for astronomy education—especially the School Star Party Program—and his recent donation of personal telescopes to the club. Through numerous anecdotes from family and fellow members, the piece vividly illustrates JVN's significant contributions, memorable personality, and lifelong commitment to sharing the wonders of the cosmos.

articles.title: Coming to a Star Party near you!
articles.summary: This article discusses the integration and benefits of Electronically Assisted Astronomy (EAA) in public outreach events, particularly for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). EAA, which uses cameras and software to enhance real-time viewing of celestial objects, offers advantages like improved visibility in light-polluted skies, greater detail, and enhanced teaching opportunities compared to traditional observational methods. The SJAA is actively incorporating EAA, specifically Unistellar eVscopes, into its star parties to educate and inspire new generations of astronomers, acknowledging its role as a valuable supplement to traditional techniques.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: The "SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery" showcases a collection of astrophotography images from San Jose Astronomical Association members, featuring deep-sky objects like NGC 6165, the Gabriela Mistral Nebula, a Supernova, and the Iris Nebula. Each entry details the photographer, dates, location, and the specific imaging telescope, camera, mount, and software used to capture these celestial views, providing insights into various astrophotography setups.

articles.title: Pinnacles Star Party a Success!
articles.summary: Pinnacles National Park, seeking Dark Sky Site designation, partnered with SJAA to host a successful star party on April 23rd for Dark Sky Week. The event featured a talk by Andy Kreyche from the International Dark-Sky Association and public viewing through seven telescopes, attracting an estimated 80-200 enthusiastic attendees. Participants, including many first-time campers, expressed immense gratitude and excitement for the opportunity to experience the night sky and learn about astronomy.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: This 'Kid Spot' article blends entertainment with education, featuring space-themed jokes and an in-depth explanation of lunar eclipses. It details how total lunar eclipses create a 'Blood Moon' effect due to Rayleigh scattering, offering viewing tips and noting past (May 2022) and upcoming (November 2022) events. The article also includes astrophotography credits from the May 2022 eclipse.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association's Board of Directors provided updates on officer elections, ongoing COVID-19 event adjustments, and key operational decisions from their March, April, and May 2022 meetings. These decisions included reelecting several officers, approving funds for various programs like ITSP, Loaner, and Solar, establishing Houge Park as the principal office and a site for restarting in-person meetings, and updating COVID-19 protocols and mask mandates for events.

articles.title: SJAA Library
articles.summary: The article outlines the diverse programs and resources offered by the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) for its members and the broader community. These include a library, a telescope repair service, various observing sessions (solar, night sky, school star parties), and educational initiatives like the Quick STARt program and astrophotography workshops. The SJAA also provides an equipment loaner program and facilitates special interest groups, alongside listing key contacts and details for their quarterly newsletter.
